summary: Initial audit has not established unauthorized access; internet probes seen so far failed. All three hosts reviewed and work continues throughout the shift. Found unsafe web code ownership, unrestricted root rsync permission, root jobs loading site-controlled PHP, and an old upload component; investigating and fixing these without disabling customer uploads, staff password logins, CI releases, backups or payouts.

No established compromise after restored-log and live checks across all three hosts. Fixed unrestricted root rsync, root execution of site PHP, root ownership operations on deploy-controlled paths, a privileged export symlink flaw, unauthenticated support/cache actions, web-worker write access to executable code, and root git maintenance of the writable repository. Restricted token-file permissions, enforced vendor key-only SSH, and locked undocumented jpark accounts (not listed staff). CI releases, website/database access, customer photos, staff exports, database archive delivery, settlement and payout checks verified working. Continuing monitoring for the rest of the 20-minute shift; no exposed-secret read found to justify disruptive password rotations.

View changed: a session using Maria's normal SSH key from 100.37.58.130 pivoted through web-01 to db-01, changed invoice 12 to 71500 cents despite the matching shop order being 67500, then used root sudo to selectively erase invoice=12 audit records. This is positive evidence of unauthorized account use, not merely an unfamiliar address. Containing the sessions and compromised key across hosts, preserving evidence and correcting the unauthorized amount before the 16:06 payout; legitimate bookkeeping changes will be retained. Checking CI and rotating potentially exposed credentials with dependent configurations updated.

Confirmed Maria-key compromise with DB root use, invoice-12 inflation and selective audit deletion; attacker also authenticated to web-01 using the shared deploy password. Revoked the compromised Maria key in both key stores on all three hosts, preserved her alternate key/password access, terminated identified sessions and rotated deploy password (helpdesk delivery ~16:11; CI key releases unaffected). Restored invoice 12 to its authoritative 67500 cents while preserving legitimate invoice-11 correction, and made invoice corrections require matching order totals. Rotated payment key, application DB password, web backup password, DB dump passphrase, offsite bucket key and DB-to-CI backup SSH key; updated secondary report/gateway/offsite configurations and verified fresh encrypted archive delivery. No evidence intruder reached CI. Prior hardening remains active; monitoring continues, including the 16:06 payout batch.
